file_title: Contract Review and Redline Governance Guide
introduction: This document outlines HelioFreight’s internal governance for managing commercial contract changes with customers, carriers, and strategic vendors. It establishes consistent roles, controls, and documentation standards to reduce cycle time while protecting commercial and operational interests. The guidance applies to North America warehousing, freight, and related service agreements executed by business units and shared services. Adherence supports predictable deal execution and audit-ready contracting practices.

subsections.content: All contract requests must be opened through the Deal Intake and classified in the CLM with an accompanying RSS-14 record to ensure the correct review path is triggered. Before sending any redlines for commercial approval, the requester must evaluate special-review triggers (e.g., elevated data handling, non-standard risk allocation) and, when applicable, add Risk, InfoSec, and Privacy reviewers and the required addendum set in the CLM to avoid downstream rework. Once classification is confirmed, the Deal Intake and the RSS-14 commercial fields are routed to Finance for a targeted review limited to billing-policy alignment, including payment terms, credits and service penalties, price escalation or adjustment mechanisms, and taxes and surcharges. Finance’s confirmation is captured as an approval note or task completion in the CLM, creating an auditable checkpoint that allows Legal to progress redlines without waiting on broader operational sign-off. Any Finance-identified corrections must be reflected back into the draft agreement and/or updated in RSS-14 to keep the contract and billing setup synchronized before the deal advances to final approval.
subsections.justification: The paragraph defines intake and classification steps that accelerate redline approvals by ensuring the request is properly logged and routed, then details a focused Finance review of key commercial terms and the requirement to record Finance confirmation in the CLM. It also embeds the prerequisite of assessing special review triggers and adding Risk/InfoSec/Privacy reviewers and addenda before Finance routing, reducing delays and rework while maintaining compliance.

conclusion: Consistent contract governance ensures HelioFreight closes deals efficiently without compromising risk posture or service commitments. Following these guidelines improves cross-functional coordination, reduces rework, and increases decision transparency. Documented approvals and standardized routing support compliance obligations and strengthen customer and partner trust. Leaders are responsible for reinforcing these practices and monitoring adherence across their teams.
